title: Forty Shillings a Day: The Solar Kit M-KOPA Sold Through M-Pesa
conflicts: Launch date: commercial sales from June 2012 (Bloomberg Oct 2012, London Business School) vs 'late 2012' (CNBC) vs operations starting about November 2012 (Business Daily, '15 months ago' in Feb 2014); story says sales began in June and opens on the October 2012 Eldoret/Kitale rollout (ITWeb). Founding year 2011 (LBS) vs 2012 (How we made it in Africa) vs 2010 start-up (Wikipedia); story gives no founding year. Prices changed over time (2012: 2,500 deposit + 40/day, 16,900 total; 2014: 2,999 + 50/day; 2015-16: ~$35 deposit, ~$29 per SSIR); only 2012 figures used. Customer counts consistent over time (1,000 / 50,000 / 150,000 / 300,000+); story stops at 300,000.
notes: Funding changed from venture to mixed: first backers were Gray Ghost Ventures (impact VC) plus Shell Foundation and DFID grants, later CBA and Gates Foundation loans. Founder words: Moore (Bloomberg 2012, ITWeb 2012, TechCrunch 2016) and Hughes's later recollection of dropping renting and hourly charging (How we made it in Africa 2016), attributed as later. Quote stance: complicates (trust vs the SIM switch-off).
